source.title: A Weight Initialization Based on the Linear Product Structure for Neural Networks
source.authors: Qipin Chen; Wenrui Hao; Jun-Cai He

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full 19-page paper; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares LPS and He initialization and reports how often training avoids collapse in small fully connected ReLU networks, bearing on initialization and trainability. It does not measure the claim's CIFAR training-error outcome or the specific initialization methods in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports validation error rates for MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, but these are not training classification error or training speed. The CIFAR validation results are not rows for the versions listed. Figure 1 reports dying-ReLU probabilities, but exact values are shown only in the figure; the text states the comparison qualitatively.
record.test_reason: The study uses variance-based initialization principles to develop LPS and evaluates its performance against He initialization. Its training results measure avoidance of collapse at fixed architectures, not learning speed or attainable training depth as specified in V4. Initialization-only output variance and benchmark validation errors also do not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they present LPS as a complement to existing initialization methods, particularly for dying ReLUs, and claim feasibility and efficiency on benchmarks. Their probability-one avoidance claim is asymptotic in the number of reinitializations, not a finite-run guarantee. They explicitly acknowledge that non-collapse does not guarantee zero loss and that excessive reinitialization can remove useful nonlinearity. Their claim about finding all minima derives from polynomial-system homotopy theory; the reported LPS experiments do not demonstrate exhaustive recovery of the original networks' minima.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces LPS initialization and compares it with He initialization; it does not test the initialization methods or comparisons specified in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: In the function-approximation experiments, non-collapse rates vary with the target function and number of LPS reinitializations. Figure 1 also varies network depth, but exact plotted values are not extractable from the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: LPS increases post-training non-collapse frequency over He across four regression tasks, with strong dependence on target function and reinitialization count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and selective reinitialization affect collapse frequency in narrow deep ReLU regression networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports lower born-dead frequency with LPS than He across network depths, using output variance before training; numerical plot values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LPS reduces the probability of nearly constant outputs at initialization in narrow feedforward ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Benchmark comparisons report validation error, validation-accuracy threshold frequencies, and lowest validation errors across initialization runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization choice affects validation performance and its variability in the tested benchmark architectures.

record.problems: Function-approximation experiments use narrow networks and a non-collapse measure, not classification error or training speed. Table 1 reports percentages without uncertainty estimates. The benchmark comparisons report validation error, not training error. Figure 1 values are presented graphically without recoverable exact numbers in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 1 results were omitted. CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 and other benchmark validation-error results were left out because they are not training classification error, training speed, or trainable-depth measurements named by the versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and dependencies on size, stopping, or regularization.
Gradient-descent convergence to spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain versus residual convolutional networks; deep plain tanh training and normalization-free residual training.

Learning speed and successfully trainable depth under activation-matched initialization; signal and gradient propagation across layers; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and 10,000-layer convolutional training. He initialization is a comparator, but the reported non-collapse measure does not test these outcomes.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to stability thresholds.
Accuracy gain per training time or epoch and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 percentages and architecture assignments match the supplied text. Complete their conditions with Adam, learning rate 0.001, and 4,000 training steps. Appendix Table 6 gives collapse thresholds of 0.09 for f1 and 0.2 for f2–f4; these differ from Figure 1's initialization-only output-variance threshold of 1e-10. A high non-collapse percentage is not a measured rate of accurate fitting, and a low percentage is not evidence against V4's conditional signal-preservation claim.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size or training duration.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks as a function of depth, and normalization removal.
The specified Glorot, He, Schoenholz, Pennington and Xiao initialization comparisons; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights; training speed; and 10,000-layer networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Four tested function-approximation networks; LPS versus He, across reported reinitialization counts
reader_labels.reason: LPS produced higher non-collapse percentages than He in all four functions, though this is not a direct measure of learning speed or trainable depth (R1–R36).
